speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are a newborn presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting; I need to clarify your history to ensure your safety. How many hours old were you when these symptoms first began, and has the vomiting been forceful or projectile?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Malrotation with Volvulus.

The history of bilious vomiting starting within six hours of birth, combined with a family history of pyloric stenosis and maternal missed prenatal visits (risking undiagnosed anatomic issues), makes this an emergency. I am requesting an urgent Abdominal Ultrasound and a STAT Upper GI series to confirm the diagnosis immediately.
